text:
maria_support: FYI customer opened a ticket — embeddings endpoint returning 768-dim vectors for them while their pipeline expects 1536. Also saw a billing spike. sharing their request + logs below, looks like a client-side shape issue.

ajay_se: can you paste the raw request body they sent and the Content-Type header?

maria_support: pasted from customer (they redacted key):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n  -d '{"input":"[\"Hello world\"]","model":"text-embedding-3-small"}'
```

maria_support: note: they accidentally stringified the array into the input field. they said sometimes they send a single string, sometimes already-array depending on code path.

ajay_se: that explains it — our runtime treats a string input as a single scalar item -> uses the small model routing, and their downstream expects the large model dims (1536). also nested/stringified arrays can break our batching layer and cause extra retries.

dave_sre: pulled request_id 2028-09-08/req-8f3 from logs. inbound body was parsed as a string. our batching saw 1 item -> routed to small. billing counted as 1 request for small model but their downstream validator expected large dims and flagged mismatch, then retried with the larger model which created the billing spike.

ajay_se: repro snippet (JS anti-pattern we see):
```js
// BAD: double-encoded input -> server sees a string not array
const payload = {
  input: JSON.stringify([textSnippet]),
  model: 'text-embedding-3-large'
}
fetch('/v1/embeddings', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Authorization': 'Bearer KEY'},
  body: JSON.stringify(payload)
})
```

ajay_se: correct approach:
```js
// GOOD: pass raw array, let JSON.stringify at top level do the job
const payload = {
  input: [textSnippet],
  model: 'text-embedding-3-large'
}
fetch('/v1/embeddings', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Authorization': 'Bearer KEY'},
  body: JSON.stringify(payload)
})
```

maria_support: also saw customers using axios with `data: JSON.stringify({ input: JSON.stringify([...]) })` same problem. will add that to KB.

dave_sre: quick debug info from our side (sanitized):
```
INBOUND req-8f3 parsed_input_type=string model_requested=text-embedding-3-large routed_model=text-embedding-3-small embedding_dim=768 expected_dim_hint=1536 billing_tokens=XXX
```

ajay_se: recommended reply to customer: 1) ensure `input` is an array (not a JSON string) 2) confirm Content-Type: application/json and you're passing a JS array/object to JSON.stringify only once 3) if using SDK, update to latest — older SDK had a bug that auto-stringified singletons. 4) send the failing request_id so we can validate billing and issue credits if needed.

maria_support: drafted reply ready, offering to refund excess tokens for the two affected days and will provide a short code example.

ops-bot: escalation created -> eng-runtime ticket #ENG-1547 assigned to ajay_se for batching/edge-case hardening.

ajay_se: followup action: add a guard in parsing to treat stringified-json arrays as arrays if they parse cleanly, and log a clearer client-warning response (400 with hint) to reduce customer confusion.

maria_support: thanks — I'll send the patch note + credit offer to customer and ask for the request_id. closing after confirmation. :thumbsup:
